name: 3/4 in Bull Rope Rigging Sling
title: 3/4 in Bull Rope Rigging Sling for Tree Removal
meta: A 3/4 in bull rope rigging sling for heavy tree removal: spliced eye, choke or basket hitch, and a big working margin for blocking down large wood.
tagline: Heavy spliced bull rope sling for setting blocks and choking big wood on removals.
summary: A 3/4 in bull rope rigging sling is the workhorse for hanging a block or choking a heavy pick on large removals. Bull rope construction gives it the strength and some of the stretch you want when wood is being let run and caught.
highlights: 3/4 in bull rope construction for heavy rigging
Spliced eye for clean choker or basket hitches
Pairs with large rigging blocks and lowering devices
Rope sling is lighter and kinder to bark than chain
Easy to inspect along its whole length
specs: Block slings, chokers on heavy picks

body.h: Where a 3/4 in sling earns its place
p: When the wood gets big, the sling holding the rigging block is the piece everything hangs on. A 3/4 in bull rope sling has the bulk and strength to anchor a large block on a spar, or to choke a long top that will be lowered on a heavy line. The spliced eye lets you girth hitch it around the stem, or run a choker so the sling cinches as load comes on.

Rope slings grip bark well, pack down in a gear bag, and do not chew up the tree the way chain can. They also let you see and feel damage as you coil them. Browse the full heavy-duty slings range to match sling size to your block and rigging line.

Check the eye splice and the whole body for cuts, pulled strands, glazing from friction, and hard or crunchy spots. Chainsaw nicks are the most common damage, so keep slings clear of the cut. Rigging gear takes shock loads that can far exceed the weight of the piece, so size slings with a generous working load margin, inspect before every use, and retire any sling that is cut, glazed, melted or crushed. Rigging should be planned and run by trained crews working to ANSI Z133.
Store slings dry and out of sun, and keep them away from bar oil and fuel, which weaken fibers over time.

faq.q: Is a 3/4 in sling overkill for most removals?
faq.a: For limbing and small pieces, yes. It is meant for heavy blocking down and large tops, where a lighter sling would have too little margin.

faq.q: Can I use a bull rope sling as a choker?
faq.a: Yes. Run the tail through the eye so it cinches on the stem, and make sure the hitch sits where it cannot slide off the end of the piece.

name: 3/4 in Tenex-TEC Dead-Eye Rigging Sling
title: 3/4 in Tenex-TEC Dead Eye Rigging Sling
meta: Heavy 3/4 in dead eye rigging sling spliced from Samson Tenex-TEC. Quick to choke on a spar, holds blocks and natural-crotch rigging on big tree removals.
tagline: Single-eye Tenex-TEC sling for choking spars and hanging blocks on heavy removals.
summary: This 3/4 in dead eye rigging sling is spliced from Samson Tenex-TEC, a firm 12-strand polyester that holds its shape and resists abrasion. The single eye lets you choke it on a spar in seconds and clip or tie off the tail to a block or ring.
highlights: 3/4 in Samson Tenex-TEC 12-strand polyester
Dead-eye design: one spliced eye, open tail
Chokes tight on spars and leaders
Firm braid resists snagging and abrasion
Suited to large blocks and heavy rigging lines

body.h: How a dead eye sling works
p: A dead eye sling has one spliced eye and a plain tail. Wrap the tail around the stem, pass it through the eye, and it cinches down as the load comes on. The tail can then be tied to a block, threaded through a ring, or used to back up a natural crotch. It is quick to set, quick to remove, and easy to adjust for stem diameter.

Tenex-TEC is a tight 12-strand polyester. It stretches less than nylon, stands up to bark abrasion, and is easy to inspect strand by strand. See our heavy-duty rigging slings for other diameters and configurations.

Look for cut or pulled strands, flattened or glazed sections where the sling rode against the stem, and any slipping in the splice. Retire a sling with damage in the eye or splice, since that is where it carries load. Rigging gear takes shock loads that can far exceed the weight of the piece, so size slings with a generous working load margin, inspect before every use, and retire any sling that is cut, glazed, melted or crushed. Rigging should be planned and run by trained crews working to ANSI Z133.
Wash off grit when needed, dry it in shade, and keep it apart from chainsaw fuel and bar oil.

faq.q: What is the difference between a dead eye and an eye-and-eye sling?
faq.a: A dead eye has one eye and a free tail that you tie or choke. An eye-and-eye has two spliced eyes and is used girth hitched or with a carabiner or shackle.

faq.q: Is Tenex-TEC good for rigging slings?
faq.a: Yes. It is a firm, low-stretch polyester braid that resists abrasion and holds a splice well, which suits a sling that gets choked on rough bark.

name: 5/8 in Bull Rope Rigging Sling
title: 5/8 in Bull Rope Sling for Arborist Rigging
meta: A 5/8 in bull rope sling for everyday arborist rigging: hang a block, choke a limb or top, and keep load off the bark. Lighter than 3/4 in, still strong.
tagline: Mid-weight spliced bull rope sling for daily blocking and limb rigging.
summary: A 5/8 in bull rope sling is the size most crews reach for on routine removals. It is strong enough for a mid-size block and heavy limbs, yet light enough to carry several on a saddle without fighting them.
highlights: 5/8 in bull rope construction
Spliced eye for choke and girth hitches
Good match for mid-size rigging blocks
Lighter to carry aloft than 3/4 in
Rope body grips bark and spares the cambium
specs: Block slings, limb and top chokers

p: Most rigging on residential removals lands in the range where 5/8 in is the right call. Use it to hang a block on a spar, choke limbs being lowered on a half-inch to five-eighths rigging line, or set a redirect. The spliced eye keeps the sling compact and lets you cinch it on stems of many sizes.
If you regularly bring down big wood, step up to 3/4 in for your block sling and keep 5/8 in for chokers. The heavy-duty slings page lists both.
Bull rope is built to be loaded and shock loaded day after day, and the slight give in it helps soften the catch when a piece is let run before it is stopped.

Run a sling through your hands before each job. Cuts, chainsaw nicks, flattened spots, glazing and stiff sections are reasons to retire it. Pay close attention to the splice. Rigging gear takes shock loads that can far exceed the weight of the piece, so size slings with a generous working load margin, inspect before every use, and retire any sling that is cut, glazed, melted or crushed. Rigging should be planned and run by trained crews working to ANSI Z133.
Keep slings in a dedicated bag so they do not soak up bar oil or fuel in the truck.

faq.q: What block does a 5/8 in sling suit?
faq.a: It suits mid-size rigging blocks used with 1/2 in to 5/8 in rigging lines. Check the block maker's sling recommendations and keep a healthy margin.

faq.q: How long does a rigging sling last?
faq.a: It depends on use and damage, not the calendar. Inspect it every time and retire it at the first sign of cuts, glazing or splice problems.

name: 9/16 in Dead-Eye Rigging Sling with Tylaska LFB-14 Basilisk
title: 9/16 in Dead Eye Sling with Tylaska LFB-14
h1: 9/16 in Dead-Eye Rigging Sling with Tylaska LFB-14 Basilisk
meta: A 9/16 in dead eye sling with Tylaska LFB-14 Basilisk hardware, ready for natural-crotch style rigging. Spliced eye, clean running surface, quick setup.
tagline: Dead-eye rigging sling paired with Tylaska low-friction hardware for redirects.
summary: This 9/16 in dead eye sling with Tylaska LFB-14 Basilisk hardware gives you a ready-made anchor with a smooth, low-friction surface for the rigging line. Choke it on a stem and the hardware sits where you want your rigging point.
highlights: 9/16 in spliced dead-eye sling
Includes Tylaska LFB-14 Basilisk hardware
Smooth running surface for the rigging line
Chokes quickly around spars and leaders
Lighter alternative to a full rigging block setup

body.h: A sling and rigging point in one
p: Pairing a dead eye sling with low-friction hardware gives you a compact rigging point you can set without hanging a full block. Choke the sling around the stem, and the Tylaska hardware gives the rigging line a smooth, rounded path that is easier on rope than running over bark. It works well for redirects and for lighter pieces where a block would be more than you need.

Because the line runs through hardware instead of a sheave, expect more friction than a pulley block. Factor that into how you set up the lowering device. Compare options in our heavy-duty slings section.
Treat the hardware as a rigging point, not a climbing anchor, unless the maker rates it for life support.

Inspect the sling for cuts, glazing and splice movement, and check the hardware for cracks, burrs and deep grooves worn by rope. Follow Tylaska's ratings and instructions for the hardware. Rigging gear takes shock loads that can far exceed the weight of the piece, so size slings with a generous working load margin, inspect before every use, and retire any sling that is cut, glazed, melted or crushed. Rigging should be planned and run by trained crews working to ANSI Z133.
Rinse grit off the hardware and let the sling dry before storing it.

faq.q: Can this replace a rigging block?
faq.a: For light to moderate pieces and redirects it often can. For heavy blocking down, a properly rated block on a heavier sling is the better choice.

faq.q: Does the hardware come off the sling?
faq.a: That depends on how the sling is built. Check the assembly when it arrives and follow the maker's guidance on removal and reuse.

name: LAND AeroPro Vented Climbing Helmet
title: LAND AeroPro Vented Climbing Helmet for Arborists
meta: The LAND AeroPro vented climbing helmet keeps tree climbers cool on long summer days. Chin strap, airflow vents and room to mount muffs and a visor.
tagline: Vented climbing-style helmet for climbers who want airflow on hot days aloft.
summary: The LAND AeroPro is a vented climbing helmet built for climbers who spend long, hot days in the canopy. Vents move air across your head and a chin strap keeps the helmet in place when you look up, lean out, or swing.
highlights: Vented shell for airflow on hot climbs
Chin strap keeps the helmet on when aloft
Climbing-style low profile
Designed to take ear muff and visor accessories
Adjustable fit

body.h: Built for time in the tree
p: A climbing helmet has to stay put. When you are hanging in a saddle, looking straight up at a tie-in point, or walking out a limb, a hard hat without a chin strap will roll off. The AeroPro uses a climbing-style fit with a chin strap so it stays on while you work. The vents let heat escape, which matters on summer pruning days when you are aloft for hours.
Pair it with helmet-mounted ear muffs and a mesh or clear visor for saw work. Before buying accessories, confirm they fit this shell.
Vented shells also shed heat when you are working in a bucket in direct sun, and a lighter helmet means less neck fatigue at the end of a long day of pruning or deadwooding.

Vented helmets are not suited to electrical work, so check what your job requires before choosing one. Any helmet used for tree work should meet the standard your employer and ANSI Z133 require, be worn as the manufacturer instructs, and be replaced after a hard impact or when the shell or suspension shows damage.
See more options in our helmet and hearing protection section, and keep the helmet out of the dashboard sun, which ages plastic quickly.

faq.q: Can I use a vented helmet near power lines?
faq.a: No. Vents compromise electrical protection. Use a helmet rated for electrical work if there is any chance of contact with conductors.

faq.q: Does the AeroPro accept ear muffs?
faq.a: It is designed for helmet accessories, but confirm the specific muff and visor fit this model before ordering.

name: LAND Safety Frontier Class E Type 2 Helmet
title: LAND Frontier Class E Type 2 Helmet for Tree Work
h1: LAND Safety Frontier Class E Type 2 Helmet
meta: The LAND Safety Frontier is a Class E Type 2 helmet for tree crews: non-vented shell for electrical-rated work plus top and side impact protection.
tagline: Non-vented Class E, Type 2 helmet for line clearance and general tree crew work.
summary: The LAND Safety Frontier is a Class E Type 2 helmet, the combination many tree crews need for line clearance and ground work. Class E refers to electrical protection, and Type 2 means the helmet is designed for both top and lateral impact.
highlights: Class E electrical rating (per the product name)
Type 2 top and side impact design
Non-vented shell
Suited to line clearance and bucket work
Adjustable suspension

body.h: Why Class E and Type 2 matter
p: In ANSI Z89.1 terms, Class E helmets are tested for electrical protection, and Type 2 helmets protect against impact to the top and sides of the head. For tree work that is a strong pairing: a limb that glances off the side of your head is just as common as one that drops straight down. Crews doing line clearance or working from a bucket near conductors often specify Class E.
Look at the label inside the shell to confirm the exact ratings of the helmet you receive.
A non-vented shell is also a good choice for ground crews feeding the chipper or running a saw on the deck, where falling debris and wet weather are a bigger concern than airflow.

Set the suspension so the helmet sits level and snug, then add a chin strap if you will be climbing or working at height. Keep paint, stickers and solvents off the shell unless the maker approves them. Any helmet used for tree work should meet the standard your employer and ANSI Z133 require, be worn as the manufacturer instructs, and be replaced after a hard impact or when the shell or suspension shows damage.
Compare it with other options in our helmets and hearing protection section.

faq.q: What does Class E Type 2 mean?
faq.a: Class E is the electrical class in ANSI Z89.1, and Type 2 means the helmet is designed for top and lateral impact. Check the label for the ratings.

faq.q: Can I climb in a Type 2 helmet?
faq.a: Many climbers do, provided it has a chin strap that keeps it secure. Follow your employer's rules and the manufacturer's instructions.

name: LIFT Radix Replacement Pad Kit
title: LIFT Radix Replacement Pad Kit for Helmets
meta: The LIFT Radix replacement pad kit restores comfort and fit in a sweat-worn helmet. Swap out flattened, smelly pads in minutes and keep the helmet in use.
tagline: Fresh comfort pads for the LIFT Radix helmet when the old ones are flat or worn.
summary: The LIFT Radix replacement pad kit swaps out the comfort pads inside your helmet once they are flattened, stained or starting to smell. Fresh pads bring back a snug fit and make long days under the helmet more comfortable.
highlights: Replacement comfort pads for the LIFT Radix
Restores snug, even fit
Quick swap without tools
Lets you keep a sound helmet in service
Worth keeping a spare set in the truck

p: Comfort pads soak up sweat every day, and after a season they compress, harden, or come loose. That changes how the helmet sits on your head, and a helmet that rocks or rides high is one you end up adjusting all day. Swapping the pads is a cheap fix that brings the fit back.
Pads do not affect the helmet's impact rating the way the shell and suspension do, but a good fit keeps the helmet where it should be when something hits it.

Fresh pads also help keep the helmet clean and cut down on the smell that builds up in a helmet worn all summer. Keeping a spare kit in the truck means you can swap them mid-season without waiting on an order.

Peel or unclip the old pads, clean the inside of the shell with mild soap and water, and let it dry. Press the new pads into the same positions and check the fit before you go back to work. Any helmet used for tree work should meet the standard your employer and ANSI Z133 require, be worn as the manufacturer instructs, and be replaced after a hard impact or when the shell or suspension shows damage.
For a full refresh, replace the suspension too. Both are listed in our helmets and hearing protection section.

faq.q: Will these pads fit other LIFT helmets?
faq.a: They are made for the Radix. Check compatibility before fitting them to any other model.

faq.q: How often should helmet pads be replaced?
faq.a: Replace them when they flatten, tear or will not come clean. With daily use that is often once or twice a year.

name: LIFT Radix Replacement Suspension Kit
title: LIFT Radix Suspension Replacement Kit
meta: Replace a worn helmet harness with the LIFT Radix suspension kit. A fresh suspension restores fit and the helmet's shock absorbing system. Fits the Radix.
tagline: Replacement suspension for the LIFT Radix when the harness is worn or damaged.
summary: The LIFT Radix suspension kit replaces the harness that holds the shell off your head. The suspension is part of how a helmet manages impact, so a cracked, stretched or brittle one should be replaced.
highlights: Replacement suspension for the LIFT Radix
Restores fit and impact absorbing clearance
Replaces cracked or stretched harness parts
Keeps a sound shell in service
Installs without tools

p: The shell spreads a blow, but the suspension holds the shell away from your skull and absorbs part of the energy. Over time, sweat, UV and constant adjusting make plastic brittle and straps stretch. When the clips no longer lock firmly, a strap is cracked, or the shell sits low on your head, it is time for a new suspension.
Many helmet makers recommend replacing the suspension on a regular schedule even when it looks fine. Follow LIFT's guidance for the Radix.

Replacing the suspension is also the right move if someone else has been wearing your helmet and stretched the fit, or if a clip has broken off. It costs a fraction of a new helmet and takes a few minutes.

Unclip the old suspension from the shell, clip in the new one at each attachment point, and adjust the ratchet and height so the helmet sits level. Check every clip is fully seated before wearing it. Any helmet used for tree work should meet the standard your employer and ANSI Z133 require, be worn as the manufacturer instructs, and be replaced after a hard impact or when the shell or suspension shows damage.
Pads and other helmet parts are in our helmets and hearing protection section.

faq.q: How do I know the suspension needs replacing?
faq.a: Replace it if any part is cracked, brittle, stretched, or no longer locks, after a hard impact, or on the schedule the manufacturer gives.

faq.q: Does a new suspension fix a damaged shell?
faq.a: No. If the shell is cracked, gouged or has taken a hard hit, replace the whole helmet.

name: Pfanner Protos Neck Guard
title: Pfanner Protos Neck Guard: Sun and Debris Cover
meta: The Pfanner Protos neck guard covers the back of your neck from sun, sawdust and rain. Attaches to the Protos helmet and keeps chips out of your collar.
tagline: Clip-on neck cover for the Protos helmet that blocks sun, chips and rain.
summary: The Pfanner Protos neck guard hangs from the back of the Protos helmet and covers your neck from sun, sawdust and rain. It is a simple add-on that makes a long day of cutting, chipping or climbing more comfortable.
highlights: Made for the Pfanner Protos helmet
Shades the back of the neck
Keeps sawdust and chips out of your collar
Helps shed light rain
Removable when you do not need it

body.h: A small add-on that pays off
p: Sawdust down the back of your shirt and a sunburned neck are two of the small things that wear a crew down by mid-afternoon. The Protos neck guard covers that gap below the helmet brim. It is useful on the ground running a saw, bucking under an open sky, and up in the tree when chips are raining down from your own cuts.
It attaches to the Protos shell, so it moves with the helmet instead of flapping loose like a bandana.

On cold, wet days it also keeps rain from running down your back, which makes a real difference when you are working all day in the weather. When it is not needed, it comes off and folds into a pocket or gear bag. The guard is a comfort item rather than protective equipment, so it does not change how the helmet protects you.

Check that the guard does not interfere with ear muffs or the chin strap once it is fitted, and keep it clear of the saw when you look over your shoulder. Wash it with mild soap and let it dry in the shade.
More helmet accessories and hearing protection are in our hearing protection section.

faq.q: Does the neck guard fit other helmets?
faq.a: It is designed for the Pfanner Protos. Fit on other helmets is not assured.

faq.q: Will it get in the way of ear muffs?
faq.a: It is made to work with the Protos system, but check clearance with your muffs and chin strap when you first fit it.

name: Removable Hook Step for Bucket Trucks
title: Removable Hook Step for Bucket Trucks
h1: Removable Hook Step for Bucket Trucks
meta: A removable hook step gives you a solid foothold to climb into a bucket or onto a truck bed. Hooks on when you need it, comes off for travel or storage.
tagline: Hook-on step for getting in and out of a bucket or truck bed safely.
summary: A removable hook step gives you a solid foothold when climbing into a bucket, onto a truck bed, or up to a chip box. It hooks on where you need it and comes off for road travel or when it would be in the way.
highlights: Hooks on and comes off without tools
Gives a stable foothold for climbing in
Helps reduce strains from awkward climbs
Stows easily in the truck
Useful on buckets, beds and chip boxes

p: Climbing in and out of a bucket or up onto a truck bed dozens of times a day is a common source of slips and strained knees. A proper step puts your foot on a flat, solid surface instead of a tire, a bumper edge or a wet lip. Because it hooks on, you can put it exactly where you need it and pull it off when the boom is moving or when you hit the road.
Check the fit on your bucket rim or truck edge before you rely on it, since lips and wall thicknesses vary.
A good step also cuts down on wear on the bucket lip and the truck body from boots scuffing their way up. Store it with the bucket gear so it is always on hand when the crew needs it.

Keep three points of contact while climbing, clean mud and chainsaw oil off the tread, and make sure the step is fully seated before you put weight on it. Never leave it hooked where it could catch a boom, a conductor or a passing vehicle. Bucket operators should be trained and follow the lift maker's instructions.
See our bucket truck accessories for covers and other add-ons.

faq.q: Will the hook step fit my bucket?
faq.a: It fits many bucket rims and truck edges, but check the hook opening against your equipment before ordering.

faq.q: Should I leave it on while driving?
faq.a: No. Remove it for road travel and whenever the boom is moving so it cannot fall or catch on anything.

name: Weaver Bucket Truck Cover, One-Man Bucket
title: Weaver Bucket Truck Cover for One-Man Buckets
h1: Weaver Bucket Truck Cover, One-Man Bucket
meta: A Weaver bucket truck cover for one-man buckets keeps rain, leaves and debris out between jobs. Tough cover protects the liner and the gear you leave inside.
tagline: Fitted cover that keeps rain and debris out of a one-man aerial bucket.
summary: The Weaver bucket truck cover fits a one-man bucket and keeps rain, leaves and sawdust out between jobs. A dry bucket is safer to step into and kinder to the tools you keep inside it.
highlights: Sized for one-man aerial buckets
Keeps rain and debris out overnight and on the road
Protects tools stored in the bucket
Helps keep the floor dry and less slippery
From Weaver, a long-time maker of arborist gear

p: An uncovered bucket fills with rainwater, leaves, and whatever drops off the trees you park under. Standing water rusts tools, soaks gloves and rope, and makes the floor slick when you step in the next morning. A fitted cover keeps all that out, and it keeps your pole saw, hand saw and lanyard out of sight on the road and at the yard.
Measure your bucket before ordering. One-man buckets vary in size between lift makers.

A cover also cuts UV damage to the bucket liner and the fiberglass, and it stops the bucket from turning into a nest for leaves and wasps over a slow week. On a cold morning, a dry bucket floor means fewer slips getting in. Covers are a small cost next to replacing ruined rope, gloves and saws.

Pull the cover over the rim and secure it so wind at highway speed cannot lift it. Shake off debris before removing it so leaves do not fall into the bucket. Take it off before operating the boom, and never use the cover as a step or a load-bearing surface.
Check the fasteners and the fabric for wear at the corners now and then, and replace a torn cover before it blows off on the highway.
Find steps, scabbards and more in our bucket truck accessories section.

faq.q: Will it fit a two-man bucket?
faq.a: No. This version is sized for one-man buckets. Measure your bucket and choose the matching cover.

faq.q: Can I drive with the cover on?
faq.a: Yes, that is one of its jobs, as long as it is secured so the wind cannot pull it off.

name: AE Fiberglass Inside-Mount Bucket Truck Scabbard
title: Fiberglass Inside-Mount Bucket Truck Scabbard
h1: AE Fiberglass Inside-Mount Bucket Truck Scabbard
meta: A fiberglass inside-mount bucket truck scabbard keeps your hand saw or pole saw head secure inside the bucket. Rigid, weatherproof, and out of the boom path.
tagline: Rigid fiberglass scabbard that mounts inside the bucket to hold a saw secure.
summary: This fiberglass inside-mount bucket truck scabbard gives your saw a fixed home inside the bucket. It keeps the blade covered and out of the way while you work, and stops a loose saw from sliding around underfoot.
highlights: Mounts inside the bucket
Rigid fiberglass body
Keeps the blade covered and secure
Frees up space on the bucket floor
Shrugs off rain and sap
specs: Hand saw or pole saw blade

p: In a bucket, a hand saw or pole saw head that is not stowed ends up on the floor, where you step on it or catch a boot on the teeth. An inside-mount scabbard keeps the blade sheathed and pointing down within easy reach. Mounting it inside the bucket keeps it clear of limbs and the boom, and away from anything you might snag when you swing in close to a stem.
Fiberglass is rigid, so the blade cannot cut through the wall, and it stands up to weather.

Keeping the saw in a fixed spot also means you always know where it is. That saves time on every cut, and it means the saw is not dropped from the bucket because it was perched on the rim. Many line clearance crews run a scabbard on every bucket in the fleet.

Check where it will sit before drilling or strapping anything to the bucket, and follow your lift maker's rules on modifying the bucket or liner. Some buckets carry a dielectric rating that must not be compromised. Bucket work near conductors requires trained, qualified operators working to ANSI Z133.
Compare mounting styles in our bucket truck and aerial lift gear section.

faq.q: What fits in this scabbard?
faq.a: It is meant for a hand saw or pole saw blade. Check the inside length and opening against your saw.

faq.q: Can I drill my bucket to mount it?
faq.a: Only if your lift maker allows it. Drilling can affect a bucket's dielectric rating, so check first.

name: SafeTree Bucket Truck Scabbard, Outside Mount
title: SafeTree Scabbard for Bucket Trucks, Outside Mount
h1: SafeTree Bucket Truck Scabbard, Outside Mount
meta: This SafeTree scabbard mounts outside a bucket truck bucket and holds a pruning saw, so the inside stays clear and the blade stays covered and in reach.
tagline: Outside-mount saw scabbard that keeps the bucket interior clear for the operator.
summary: The SafeTree scabbard for the outside of a bucket truck bucket holds a pruning or pole saw blade where you can reach it without giving up room inside. The blade stays sheathed and off the floor.
highlights: Mounts on the outside of the bucket
Keeps the bucket interior clear
Covers the blade between cuts
Easy reach while working
Built for daily line clearance and pruning work
specs: Pruning saw or pole saw blade

p: One-man buckets do not leave much room for your feet, a chainsaw, and a saw on the floor. An outside-mount scabbard moves the hand saw out of the way while keeping the handle within reach. Pull the saw, make the cut, and drop it back in without looking down.
Think about where it sits relative to the controls and the boom so it does not snag on limbs as you work in close.

Outside-mount scabbards also keep sap, sawdust and rainwater off the bucket floor, since the wet blade goes back into the scabbard rather than lying at your feet. That keeps footing better on a long day of trimming. Look at your bucket rim and the layout of your controls before deciding where it goes, and keep it on the side away from traffic when you park on the street.

Follow SafeTree's mounting instructions and your lift maker's guidance on what can be attached to the bucket. Make sure nothing you add compromises a dielectric bucket. Check the scabbard and fasteners regularly for cracks or loosening. Bucket operators should be trained and qualified for the work they do.
See our bucket truck and aerial lift gear for inside-mount options.

faq.q: Inside or outside mount: which is better?
faq.a: Outside mount saves floor space. Inside mount keeps the saw away from limbs and traffic. Many crews choose based on bucket size.

faq.q: Will it hold a pole saw head?
faq.a: It is designed for pruning saw blades. Check the length and width of your blade before ordering.

name: SafeTree Scabbard for Aerial Lifts
title: SafeTree Aerial Lift Scabbard for Pruning Saws
meta: The SafeTree aerial lift scabbard mounts a pruning saw holder to a lift basket or bucket. Keeps the blade covered, secure and in reach while you work aloft.
tagline: Saw scabbard sized for aerial lift baskets and buckets.
summary: The SafeTree aerial lift scabbard gives your pruning saw a secure, covered home on a lift basket or bucket. It keeps the blade off the floor and within reach while you are working aloft.
highlights: Mounts to aerial lift baskets and buckets
Covers the blade between cuts
Keeps the work platform clear
Quick draw and return
Made for daily pruning from a lift

p: Pruning from an aerial lift or spider lift means working in a tight platform with the controls, a chainsaw and a hand saw all within reach. A scabbard keeps the hand saw where you can grab it and stops a loose blade from sliding underfoot. It is the same idea as a saddle scabbard, adapted to a basket.
Measure the rail or wall you plan to mount it to and check it suits your platform.

A covered blade is also safer for the person working in the platform, since an exposed saw blade at knee height in a small basket is an easy way to get cut. The scabbard also keeps the teeth from being dulled by knocking around against the platform floor and rails, so the saw cuts cleaner and longer between sharpenings or blade swaps.

Mount it where it will not interfere with the controls, gates or guardrails, and check fasteners regularly. Do not drill or alter a lift's platform without the maker's approval. Lift operators should be trained, wear the fall protection the lift requires, and work to ANSI Z133.
Check the scabbard for cracks after any hard knock against a limb or stem.
More mounting options are in our bucket truck and aerial lift gear section.

faq.q: Will it fit a bucket truck as well as a lift basket?
faq.a: It is intended for aerial lift platforms and buckets, but confirm mounting fit for your specific equipment.

faq.q: Which saws fit?
faq.a: It holds a typical pruning saw blade. Check blade length against the scabbard before ordering.

name: Husqvarna 3/8 x .050 Professional Chainsaw Bar
title: Husqvarna 3/8 Chainsaw Bar, .050 Gauge, Professional
meta: Husqvarna 3/8 chainsaw bar in .050 gauge for mid to large pro saws. Replaceable sprocket nose design, built for felling, bucking and daily tree work.
tagline: Pro replacement bar in 3/8 pitch, .050 gauge for mid to large Husqvarna saws.
summary: This Husqvarna 3/8 chainsaw bar in .050 gauge is a professional replacement for mid to large saws used on removals, felling and bucking. Match the pitch, gauge, length and mount to your saw before ordering.
highlights: 3/8 in pitch, .050 in gauge
Professional-grade construction
For mid to large Husqvarna saws
Built for daily felling and bucking
Run with matching 3/8 x .050 chain

body.h: Matching the bar to your saw
p: A bar has to match three things: the saw's mount pattern, the chain pitch and the chain gauge. This bar runs 3/8 in pitch chain in .050 in gauge, a common pairing on mid-size and larger professional saws. Choose a length that suits the saw's power. A bar that is too long for the powerhead slows the chain in the cut and works the saw harder.
Count the drive links on your current chain or check the stamp on your old bar to get the length and chain right.

A professional-grade bar is built for daily use, with rails hardened to hold up and a nose made to take the load of long cutting days. If you run several saws, keep spare bars for each one, so a pinched or bent bar does not end the day early. Look at the drive sprocket and chain at the same time, since all three wear together.

Flip the bar each time you sharpen so the rails wear evenly, clean the groove and oil holes, and dress burrs off the rails with a flat file. Keep the oiler set so the chain throws a light mist when run against a stump. A pinched groove or blued rails mean the bar needs attention.
More bars and chain are in our chainsaw bars section.

faq.q: Will this fit my saw?
faq.a: Check your saw's bar mount and the length you need. Husqvarna bars are listed by mount, pitch and gauge, and all three must match.

faq.q: What chain goes on this bar?
faq.a: A 3/8 in pitch, .050 in gauge chain with the correct drive link count for the bar length.

name: Husqvarna .404 Sprocket Nose Chainsaw Bar
title: Husqvarna Sprocket Nose Bar for .404 Chain
meta: A Husqvarna sprocket nose bar for .404 chain on big saws and heavy wood. Built for felling and bucking large trees. Check the mount and length first.
tagline: Heavy-duty sprocket nose bar for big saws running .404 pitch chain.
summary: This Husqvarna sprocket nose bar for .404 pitch chain keeps the chain moving freely around the tip on big saws. It is built for felling and bucking large wood where .404 pitch chain is the norm.
highlights: .404 in pitch for large saws
Sprocket nose reduces friction at the tip
Built for heavy felling and bucking
For large-displacement professional saws
Pair with matching .404 chain

p: .404 pitch chain is bigger and tougher than 3/8 and is run on large saws cutting big wood: felling large removals, bucking trunk sections, and slabbing. A sprocket nose lets the chain roll around the tip instead of dragging, which keeps chain speed up and heat down on long bars. It is the setup you see on high-displacement saws.
Check the gauge and drive link count on your current chain, along with your saw's mount, before ordering.

Sprocket nose bars are also easier on chain at the tip, which matters in big wood where long cuts keep the chain loaded for minutes at a time. If you are buying a new bar, it is a good time to buy fresh chain and a new drive sprocket so everything starts out matched.

Grease the nose sprocket through the hole as the maker directs, flip the bar regularly, and keep the oil holes and groove clean. Replace the drive sprocket on the saw when you replace chain often, since a worn sprocket chews up new chain and bar rails. Felling with large saws should be done by trained operators in proper PPE.
Retire a bar with a cracked nose, spread rails or a bend you cannot correct.
See our chainsaw bars for other pitches and lengths.

faq.q: Can I run .404 on a mid-size saw?
faq.a: .404 is generally meant for large saws. Use the pitch your saw's maker specifies for its drive sprocket.

faq.q: Does a sprocket nose need maintenance?
faq.a: Yes. Grease it regularly and check for a loose or worn sprocket.

name: Husqvarna X-Force Narrow Kerf Pixel Chainsaw Bar .325 x .050
title: Husqvarna X-Force Pixel Bar .325 x .050
h1: Husqvarna X-Force Narrow Kerf Pixel Chainsaw Bar .325 x .050
meta: Husqvarna X-Force Pixel bar in .325 x .050 narrow kerf. Pairs with Pixel chain to cut a thinner kerf, so mid-size saws cut faster with less effort.
tagline: Narrow kerf X-Force bar for Husqvarna's Pixel chain on mid-size saws.
summary: The Husqvarna X-Force Pixel bar is a narrow kerf bar designed for Pixel chain in .325 pitch. Removing less wood per cut lets a mid-size saw pull a bar faster and with less effort.
highlights: Made for Husqvarna Pixel narrow kerf chain
.325 pitch, .050 gauge (per listing)
Narrow kerf means less wood removed
Helps mid-size saws cut faster
X-Force design from Husqvarna

p: Narrow kerf chain has smaller cutters and a thinner cut, so the saw removes less wood with each pass. On a mid-size saw that means a faster cut and less load on the engine, which you notice during a long day of bucking brush wood and limbing. Pixel chain only runs on a bar and sprocket built for it, so the bar, chain and drive sprocket must all match.
Confirm the sprocket on your saw is the Pixel type before switching from standard .325.

For crews that run several saws, Pixel bars and chain also mean one more set of parts to keep straight, so label spare bars and chain loops clearly. The payoff is a mid-size saw that feels livelier in the cut. Keep the oiler working and the bar groove clean, since narrow kerf chain is less forgiving of a dry bar.

Flip the bar each sharpening, clean the groove, and keep oil holes open. Sharpen Pixel chain with the file size Husqvarna specifies for it. A standard .325 file is too big. Keep a spare chain in the truck so you are not touching up a dull one in the field.
Browse more options in our chainsaw bars section.

faq.q: Can I run standard .325 chain on a Pixel bar?
faq.a: No. Pixel narrow kerf bars and chain are a matched system. Use Pixel chain and the matching drive sprocket.

faq.q: Which saws take Pixel bars?
faq.a: Mid-size Husqvarna saws set up for Pixel. Check your saw's manual or the bar's fitment listing.

name: Husqvarna H38 3/8 Mini x .043 Chainsaw Chain
title: Husqvarna H38 Chain: 3/8 Mini x .043
h1: Husqvarna H38 3/8 Mini x .043 Chainsaw Chain
meta: Husqvarna H38 chain in 3/8 mini (low profile) pitch and .043 gauge for small saws and top handles. Smooth, low-kickback cutting for pruning and limbing.
tagline: Low-profile 3/8 mini chain for small saws, top handles and pruning work.
summary: Husqvarna H38 chain is a 3/8 mini (low profile) chain in .043 gauge for small saws and many top-handle saws. It cuts smoothly with low vibration, which suits pruning and limbing in the tree.
highlights: 3/8 mini (low profile) pitch
.043 in gauge
For small saws and many top-handle saws
Smooth, low-vibration cutting
Good choice for pruning and limbing

p: 3/8 mini chain is the light, low-profile chain used on small rear-handle and top-handle saws. In .043 gauge it runs a thin kerf, so a small engine keeps its speed through the cut. That is what you want for pruning cuts aloft, limbing, and cleaning up brush, where a smooth, controlled cut matters more than raw speed.
Count drive links on your current loop or check the bar stamp to order the right length.

Low-profile chain also has guard links or bumper drive links on many versions, which helps cut down kickback. That is a big part of why it suits small saws and climbers. It cuts slower than full-size chain, but on a small saw aloft, smooth and controlled beats fast. Buy a few loops at once so a dull or damaged one can be swapped in the tree.

File with the round file size Husqvarna specifies for H38, keep cutters even, and touch up depth gauges every few sharpenings. Keep tension right: the chain should pull around the bar by hand yet not sag off the bottom. Top-handle saws are for trained climbers working aloft, not for ground use.
More chain and bars are in our chainsaw chain section.

faq.q: What file size does H38 use?
faq.a: Use the file size Husqvarna specifies for H38 on the chain box or in the saw manual.

faq.q: Will H38 fit my top-handle saw?
faq.a: Many top handles run 3/8 mini .043. Check your bar's pitch and gauge stamp and the drive link count.

name: Husqvarna H57S .404 x .063 Chainsaw Chain
title: Husqvarna .404 Chain, .063 Gauge (H57S)
meta: Husqvarna .404 chain in .063 gauge for big saws and heavy bucking. Tough chisel-style cutters hold up in large wood. Match drive links to your bar.
tagline: Heavy .404 pitch chain in .063 gauge for big saws on large wood.
summary: This Husqvarna .404 chain in .063 gauge is built for large saws felling and bucking big wood. Heavy cutters and a thick gauge stand up to long days on large removals.
highlights: .404 in pitch, .063 in gauge
For large-displacement professional saws
Tough cutters for big wood
Matches .404 x .063 bars
Order by drive link count

p: .404 chain is the heavy end of the range. It is run on big saws for felling large trees, bucking trunk wood and milling. The thick .063 gauge suits bars made for the largest saws. Chisel-style cutters cut fast in clean wood, while semi-chisel holds an edge longer in dirty or frozen wood, so check the cutter style before ordering for your conditions.
Match the drive link count to your bar length, and confirm your bar is .063 gauge.

Heavy chain also means more weight and more drag in the cut, so it pays to keep it sharp and well oiled. Running a dull .404 chain on a big saw makes the saw work far harder than it needs to, wastes fuel, and wears the bar and sprocket. Keep at least one spare loop per saw so you can swap and sharpen at lunch.

Use the round file size Husqvarna specifies for this chain and a matching depth gauge tool. Keep every cutter the same length so the chain runs straight. Replace the drive sprocket when it shows wear, and keep the bar oiled. Large saws demand trained operators wearing chaps or saw pants, boots, helmet, eye and hearing protection.
See more loops and reels in our chainsaw chain section.

faq.q: Will .404 chain fit a 3/8 bar?
faq.a: No. Pitch and gauge must match the bar and drive sprocket.

faq.q: How do I know how many drive links I need?
faq.a: Count the links on your old chain or read the stamp on the bar, which lists pitch, gauge and drive link count.

name: Husqvarna Replacement Chainsaw Bar Scabbard
title: Husqvarna Replacement Chainsaw Bar Scabbard
meta: A Husqvarna chainsaw bar scabbard covers the chain for transport and storage. Protects your hands, the truck and the cutters. Pick the size for your bar.
tagline: Bar cover that protects the chain, your hands and the truck in transport.
summary: A Husqvarna chainsaw bar scabbard slips over the bar and chain whenever the saw is not running. It protects your hands and the truck bed, and keeps the cutters from being dulled by rocks and tools.
highlights: Covers bar and chain in transport
Protects hands when carrying the saw
Keeps cutters sharp in the truck
Replacement for lost or cracked covers
Choose the length that matches your bar

p: Scabbards go missing on every crew. They get left on stumps, run over, or tossed in the brush pile. Running without one means a sharp chain banging against tools in the truck bed and a saw you have to carry carefully every time. A fresh scabbard keeps your chain sharp and your legs safe when you walk the saw to the next cut.
Pick the size that covers your full bar length.

Replacement scabbards are also worth having when you move to a new bar length, since an old short cover leaves the nose exposed. Many crews color mark their scabbards to match the saws so the right cover goes back on the right bar when the day ends.

Put the scabbard on whenever the saw is off and being moved or stored. Check that it clips or holds firmly on the bar. Keep a spare in the truck, since that is cheaper than a ruined chain. Saw operators should be trained and wear chaps or saw pants, eye, ear and head protection.
Replace a scabbard that is cracked or no longer grips the bar, since one that slides off is worse than useless.
More cases and covers are in our chainsaw cases and scabbards section.

faq.q: Which size do I need?
faq.a: Choose a scabbard that covers the full length of your bar. Check the listed bar lengths for each size.

faq.q: Will a Husqvarna scabbard fit other brands?
faq.a: Often yes if the bar length matches, but fit at the powerhead end can vary.

name: Arbortec BreatheFlex Pro Chainsaw Pants, Black
title: Arbortec BreatheFlex Pro Chainsaw Pants, Black
h1: Arbortec BreatheFlex Pro Chainsaw Pants, Black
meta: Arbortec BreatheFlex Pro chainsaw pants in black: light, stretchy saw protection that breathes, for climbers and ground crews. Check the protection label.
tagline: Light, breathable stretch chainsaw pants for climbers and ground workers.
summary: Arbortec BreatheFlex Pro chainsaw pants put saw protection into a light, stretchy, breathable trouser, here in black. They are built for climbers and ground crews who want to move freely while still wearing leg protection.
highlights: Built-in chainsaw protection
Stretch panels for climbing and kneeling
Breathable fabric for warm days
Black colorway
Made by Arbortec for tree work

p: Chaps work, but they flap, catch on limbs and get hot. Saw pants build the protective layers into the trouser, so nothing hangs loose when you are climbing, kneeling to buck, or dragging brush. The BreatheFlex Pro adds stretch and ventilation, which matter when you spend all day stepping up limbs or working through summer heat.
Check the label for the protection class and rating, and buy the size that lets the protective panel cover the front of the legs when you crouch.

BreatheFlex Pro pants are a popular choice for climbers who want saw protection without bulk. They also cut down on the snag points that chaps add when you are moving through a crown. Pick the color your crew prefers or your company requires.

Saw protection works by fibers that pull out and clog the chain, so any cut through the outer layer means the pants are done in that area. Wash them as Arbortec instructs, since the wrong detergent or heat can reduce protection. Saw pants are not a substitute for training, good technique and the other PPE ANSI Z133 calls for.
Hang saw pants to dry after wet days, and inspect them each morning for cuts, tears and worn knees before putting them on.
Compare styles and colors in our chainsaw pants section.

faq.q: Are chainsaw pants better than chaps?
faq.a: They protect the same way but fit closer, so they suit climbers and anyone who works in tight spots. Chaps are cheaper and easier to put on over other clothes.

faq.q: Can cut saw pants be repaired?
faq.a: No. Once the protective layer is cut, replace the pants. A patch does not restore protection.

name: Arbortec BreatheFlex Pro Chainsaw Pants, Blue
title: Arbortec BreatheFlex Pro Chainsaw Pants, Blue
h1: Arbortec BreatheFlex Pro Chainsaw Pants, Blue

name: Husqvarna 2-Stroke Premix Fuel, 48 Gallon Drum
title: Husqvarna 2-Stroke Fuel, 48 Gallon Drum
meta: Bulk Husqvarna 2-stroke fuel in a drum for busy tree crews. Ready-mixed, ethanol-free fuel keeps saws, blowers and pole saws running clean all season.
tagline: Bulk ready-mixed 2-stroke fuel for crews running a fleet of saws and handhelds.
summary: Husqvarna 2-stroke fuel in bulk lets a crew fill every saw, blower and pole saw from one supply of ready-mixed, ethanol-free fuel. No mixing at the pump, and no gumming from ethanol fuel sitting in a saw over the off-season.
highlights: Pre-mixed 2-stroke fuel, no measuring
Ethanol-free for cleaner running and storage
Bulk drum for crews with many saws
Same mix in every tool
Reduces fuel-related carb problems

p: Ethanol pump gas absorbs water and breaks down in storage, which leads to varnished carbs, hard starts and lean seizures. Pre-mixed, ethanol-free fuel avoids most of that. It also removes the mixing step, so no one on the crew gets the ratio wrong. For a company running a dozen saws and blowers, a drum works out cheaper per gallon than cans while keeping everything on the same fuel.
Confirm the mix ratio on the drum suits all your 2-stroke equipment.

Running the same fuel in every tool also makes troubleshooting easier. When a saw will not start, you know fuel quality is not the problem. Bulk premix is most useful for larger crews and companies with a yard where fuel can be stored safely. Smaller operations usually do better with cans or quarts, which are easier to rotate and keep fresh.

Store the drum upright in a ventilated spot away from ignition sources, use a proper drum pump, and fill approved cans. Follow local fire code rules for bulk fuel. Fuel saws on bare ground away from where you start them, and wipe up spills before starting.
Keep the bung sealed between uses so moisture and dirt stay out.
Bar oil and smaller fuel sizes are in our fluids section.

faq.q: Can I use premix in 4-stroke equipment?
faq.a: No. It contains 2-stroke oil and is only for 2-stroke engines.

faq.q: How long does premix keep?
faq.a: Ethanol-free premix keeps much longer than pump gas once opened, but follow the shelf-life guidance on the drum.

name: Hi-Viz Hardbody Felling Wedge
title: Hi-Viz Hardbody Felling Wedge for Chainsaws
meta: A hi-viz hardbody felling wedge lifts the tree off the bar and helps steer the fall. Bright color is easy to find in the brush and safe if the chain hits it.
tagline: Bright, hard plastic wedge for lifting trees and freeing pinched bars.
summary: A hi-viz hardbody felling wedge is a plastic wedge you drive into the back cut to keep it open and lift the tree toward the face. The hard body takes heavy blows, and the bright color makes it easy to find in leaves and brush.
highlights: Hard plastic body for heavy striking
Bright hi-viz color is easy to spot
Safe for the chain if you nick it
Keeps the back cut open and the bar free
Use two or more for bigger trees
specs: Back cut lifting and bar release

p: Set a wedge in the back cut as soon as there is room, and it keeps the kerf from closing and pinching the bar. Drive it further and it lifts the tree toward the face cut, which helps on trees with a slight back lean. Plastic wedges are used because a chain that touches one is not ruined, unlike steel. A hard body resists mushrooming when you hit it with an axe or sledge.
Hi-viz color matters more than people think. A wedge dropped in leaves is gone for good.

Carry a small axe or a hand sledge to drive wedges, since hitting one with the back of a saw or another wedge does damage. Keep spares in the truck, as wedges get lost under brush, buried in leaves, or split after hard use. Hard plastic wedges are cheap enough that it pays to have extras on hand.

Wedges help but they do not fix poor felling cuts or a heavy back lean. Plan the escape route, keep the hinge intact, and stack wedges or use a pull line for trees you are unsure of. Felling should only be done by trained operators.
See more sizes and styles in our felling wedges section.

faq.q: Plastic or aluminum wedge?
faq.a: Plastic is safest for the chain and the most common choice. Aluminum or magnesium is used where you need more lift and durability.

faq.q: How many wedges should I carry?
faq.a: At least two, so you can stack them or set one on each side of a large back cut.

name: Husqvarna 3/8 Depth Gauge Tool
title: Husqvarna Depth Gauge Tool for 3/8 Chain
meta: The Husqvarna depth gauge tool sets the raker height on 3/8 chain so your saw bites cleanly. Lay it on the chain, file the gauge flush, and get back to work.
tagline: Simple jointer that sets raker height on 3/8 pitch chain.
summary: A Husqvarna depth gauge tool sets the height of the rakers on 3/8 chain. Lay it on the chain, file any raker that sticks up flush with the tool, and the chain takes the right bite again.
highlights: Sets depth gauge (raker) height
Made for 3/8 pitch chain
Simple lay-on, file-flush method
Pocket size for the truck or saw kit
Use with a flat file

p: Every time you sharpen, the cutter gets lower. The depth gauge in front of it does not, so after a few sharpenings the chain stops biting and starts making dust instead of chips. Filing rakers down a little restores the bite. Too far and the chain grabs, vibrates and kicks back more easily. The depth gauge tool takes out the guessing.
Check your chain's raker setting with each sharpening and file when they stand proud of the tool.

A depth gauge tool is also one of the cheapest things in a saw kit, and it makes a bigger difference to cutting speed than most people expect. Set the rakers right and a chain that seemed to need replacing will often cut like new again. Keep one with the files in every saw kit so it is always at hand.

Lay the tool on the chain so the raker pokes through the slot, file it flush with a flat file, then round the front edge slightly. Work the same way on both sides. Keep the chain on the bar and the saw secure, with a stump vise if you are in the field.
Files, guides and vises are in our wrenches and files section.

faq.q: Does this work on .325 chain?
faq.a: This one is for 3/8 pitch chain. Use the tool that matches your chain's pitch.

faq.q: How often should I file depth gauges?
faq.a: Check them every sharpening, and file whenever they sit above the tool, often every three to five sharpenings.

name: Husqvarna Stump Vise
title: Husqvarna Stump Vise for Field Chain Sharpening
meta: The Husqvarna stump vise holds your bar steady for sharpening in the field. Tap it into a stump or log, clamp the bar, and file the chain right on the job.
tagline: Field vise you tap into a stump to hold the saw steady for filing.
summary: The Husqvarna stump vise holds your saw bar steady so you can sharpen on the job. Tap it into a stump or log, clamp the bar, and file the chain at a comfortable height without wrestling the saw.
highlights: Tap into any stump or log
Clamps the bar for steady filing
Helps produce more consistent sharpening
Packs into a saw kit
No bench needed

p: Filing a chain with the saw sitting loose on a tailgate gives uneven cutters and a chain that pulls to one side. A stump vise fixes that. Drive it into a stump, tighten the jaws on the bar, and the saw holds still while you file every cutter at the same angle and length. It is the closest thing to a bench vise you can carry in your pocket.
Pick a solid stump at a height that lets you stand comfortably over the saw.

A stump vise also keeps you from filing with the saw balanced on your knee, which is both bad for the chain and a good way to get cut. It is small enough to keep in a saw kit or chap pocket, so you can sharpen whenever the chain gets dull rather than putting it off until the end of the day.

Clamp on the bar, not the chain, and leave enough room for the file to pass. Stop the engine and set the chain brake before sharpening. Knock the vise out of the stump when you finish so it does not get left behind or catch a saw later.
Files, guides and gauges are in our wrenches and files section.

faq.q: Will it hold any bar?
faq.a: It clamps most standard saw bars. Very thin bars may need care to grip evenly.

faq.q: Can I use it on a log?
faq.a: Yes. Any solid piece of wood you can drive it into works.

name: Pferd Chain Sharp CS-X Filing Guide
title: Pferd Chain Sharp CS-X: 2-in-1 Filing Guide
h1: Pferd Chain Sharp CS-X Filing Guide
meta: The Pferd Chain Sharp CS-X files the cutter and depth gauge in one stroke. A fast, consistent way to sharpen chain in the field. Match it to your pitch.
tagline: 2-in-1 guide that files cutter and raker together in a single stroke.
summary: The Pferd Chain Sharp CS-X is a 2-in-1 filing guide that sharpens the cutter and lowers the depth gauge in the same stroke. It is a quick way to keep a chain sharp and consistent in the field.
highlights: Files cutter and depth gauge at once
Holds round and flat files at set angles
Fast, repeatable field sharpening
Sized by chain pitch
Replacement files available

p: Sharpening by hand means filing each cutter, then going back with a depth gauge tool and flat file. The CS-X combines the two. The guide holds a round file for the cutter and a flat file for the raker, so each stroke sharpens and sets depth together. That keeps cutters and rakers in step, which means a chain that cuts straight and smooth.
Buy the guide that matches your chain pitch. The files and angles are set for that size.

The guide is a good fit for crews where several people sharpen chains, since it takes much of the guessing out of the job and keeps chains closer to factory spec. It also helps newer climbers and ground workers learn what a properly sharpened chain looks like and how it should cut. Keep it in a case so the files stay sharp and clean.

Clamp the bar in a vise, set the chain brake, and lay the guide on the chain with the arrow toward the nose. File with firm, even strokes away from you, the same count on each cutter, then flip sides. Replace the files when they start to glaze or slip.
See more sharpening gear in our wrenches and files section.

faq.q: Which CS-X do I need?
faq.a: Choose by chain pitch and file size. Check the size printed on your chain box or in your saw manual.

faq.q: Can I replace the files?
faq.a: Yes. Replacement round and flat files are sold to fit the guide.

name: Timber Savage Flat File
title: Timber Savage Chainsaw Flat File for Rakers
meta: The Timber Savage chainsaw flat file takes depth gauges down to height and dresses burrs off bar rails. A basic tool every saw kit needs alongside a round file.
tagline: Flat file for lowering rakers and cleaning up bar rails.
summary: The Timber Savage flat file is a chainsaw flat file for taking depth gauges down to height and dressing burrs off bar rails. It is the other half of a sharpening kit, next to your round file.
highlights: Lowers depth gauges (rakers)
Dresses burrs off bar rails
Use with a depth gauge tool
Fits a saw kit or chap pocket
Basic sharpening essential

body.h: What a flat file is for
p: Round files sharpen cutters. A flat file handles the rest: lowering rakers so the chain takes a proper bite, and smoothing the burrs that build up on the edges of the bar rails. Rail burrs cause the chain to bind and wear unevenly, so a few strokes with a flat file each time you flip the bar helps it last.
Use it with a depth gauge tool so you take rakers down by the right amount.

A flat file is also handy for squaring up the end of a scratched depth gauge tool, smoothing the edge of a wedge, or touching up other jobsite tools. Keep it in the saw kit with a file handle fitted, since the bare tang is sharp and hard to grip. A handle also gives you better control and steadier strokes, which means a cleaner result on the rakers and rails.

File in one direction, pushing away, and lift on the return stroke. Keep it dry and clean, and store it so it does not rattle against other steel, which dulls the teeth. Set the chain brake and clamp the bar before filing.
Round files, guides and vises are in our wrenches and files section.

faq.q: Can I sharpen cutters with a flat file?
faq.a: No. Cutters need a round file of the right diameter. The flat file is for rakers and rails.

faq.q: How often should I file the bar rails?
faq.a: Check them when you flip the bar, and dress them whenever you feel a burr.

name: Timber Savage Round Chainsaw Files
title: Timber Savage Round Chainsaw Files
meta: Timber Savage round chainsaw files for sharpening cutters in the field. Pick the diameter that matches your chain pitch and keep a sharp file in every saw kit.
tagline: Round files for sharpening chainsaw cutters, sized by chain pitch.
summary: Timber Savage round chainsaw files sharpen the cutters on your chain in the field or the shop. Choose the diameter that matches your chain, and replace files once they stop biting.
highlights: Sharpen chainsaw cutters
Choose diameter by chain type
For field and shop sharpening
Use with a file holder or guide
Keep spares in every saw kit

p: File diameter has to match the chain. Too small and you hook the cutter. Too big and you change the top-plate angle and weaken the edge. Most chains have the correct file size printed on the box or listed in the saw manual. Keep the right size for each saw on the truck, especially if the crew runs a mix of top handles, mid-size and big saws.
Use a file holder or guide to keep the file at the right height and angle.

Round files are consumables, and a worn file is one of the most common reasons a chain will not cut well even after sharpening. It slides over the cutter without removing steel and leaves a rounded edge. Buying files in packs keeps the cost down and means there is always a fresh one in the kit. Fit a file handle for better control and safer filing.

Clamp the bar, set the chain brake, and file with smooth strokes away from you, rotating the file slightly so it wears evenly. Give each cutter the same number of strokes. A file that skates instead of biting is worn out. Swap it before it costs you time.
Flat files, guides and depth gauges are in our wrenches and files section.

faq.q: What size round file do I need?
faq.a: Check the chain box or saw manual. The file size is matched to the chain's pitch and cutter.

faq.q: How long does a round file last?
faq.a: It depends on how often you sharpen. Replace it when it stops cutting cleanly, which on a busy crew can be every week or two.

name: Chipper Knife 9 x 5.5 x 5/8 in
title: Chipper Knife 9 x 5.5 x 5/8 in Replacement Blade
meta: A 9 x 5.5 x 5/8 in replacement chipper knife for brush chippers. Check your machine's knife size and bolt pattern, then keep a sharp set ready to swap.
tagline: Replacement chipper knife sized 9 x 5.5 x 5/8 in for brush chippers.
summary: This chipper knife measures 9 x 5.5 x 5/8 in and is a replacement blade for brush chippers that use that size. Sharp knives feed brush faster, use less fuel and put less strain on the machine.
highlights: 9 in long, 5.5 in wide, 5/8 in thick
Replacement blade for brush chippers
Sharp knives pull brush in faster
Keep a spare set to swap in
Confirm bolt pattern before ordering

p: Dull chipper knives beat brush instead of cutting it. The machine slows, feeds poorly, burns more fuel and passes more vibration to the bearings. Crews that keep a sharp set ready and swap knives on schedule spend less time feeding by hand. Match length, width, thickness and the bolt hole pattern to your chipper's manual before ordering.
Many crews rotate two sets: one in the machine, one at the sharpening shop.

Keeping the knives sharp also makes the chipper quieter and smoother to feed, and it cuts down on the strings of bark and fiber that wrap around the feed rollers. A sharp set produces cleaner chips that are easier to sell or spread as mulch. Write down the date of each knife change so you can plan swaps around hours of use rather than waiting until the machine starts struggling.

Shut the chipper down, remove the key, and lock the disc or drum per the maker's instructions before reaching in. Wear cut-resistant gloves, torque bolts to spec, and check the anvil gap after a knife change. Only trained crew members should service or run a chipper.
Store spare knives oiled and wrapped so the edges stay sharp and free of rust.
More chipper parts are in our chipper knives section.

faq.q: Will this knife fit my chipper?
faq.a: Check the size and bolt hole pattern in your chipper manual. Matching all dimensions and holes is essential.

faq.q: Can chipper knives be resharpened?
faq.a: Yes, usually several times, as long as you stay within the minimum width the chipper maker specifies.

title: 5 Tine Pitchfork with 54 in Fiberglass Handle
meta: A 5 tine pitchfork with a 54 in fiberglass handle for loading chips, mulch and leaves. Tough handle shrugs off weather and long days of jobsite cleanup.
tagline: Long-handled 5-tine fork for chips, mulch and brush cleanup.
summary: A 5 tine pitchfork with a 54 in fiberglass handle is the go-to tool for moving wood chips, mulch, leaves and small debris. The fiberglass handle stands up to weather and does not rot or splinter like wood.

54 in fiberglass handle

Good reach for loading trucks

p: Every tree job ends with cleanup. A 5-tine fork moves chips, mulch, leaves and small sticks faster than a shovel because material slides off less and you are not lifting dirt. The 54 in handle gives you reach when loading into a truck or chip box, and the fiberglass handle shrugs off rain, sun and being left in the bed overnight.
Use it to spread mulch at the base of trees after planting, too.

A fork with a long handle also saves your back when clearing the drop zone around a removal, since you can stand more upright while you work. Keep one on every truck. It is handy for raking small sticks off a lawn, clearing the area under a chipper, and loading the last of the chips from the street into the truck before you leave.

Lift with your legs, keep loads modest, and carry the fork tines down so they do not catch anyone. Hang it or stand it up in the truck so tines are not exposed underfoot. Check the head and handle joint for looseness now and then.
Rinse off sap and wet chips at the end of the day so the tines do not rust.
More rakes, forks and shovels are in our landscaper tools section.

faq.q: Why 5 tines instead of 3 or 4?
faq.a: More tines hold more loose material such as chips and mulch. Fewer tines suit hay and long straw.

faq.q: Is a fiberglass handle better than wood?
faq.a: It resists rot and weather and does not splinter, which suits a tool that lives in the truck.
